headline: Nvidia and Micron shares rose before Friday's market open after Bloomberg reported that OpenAI expects to reach a $70 billion yearly revenue pace by the end of 2026.
score_reason: Pool score 7 lowered by 1: the original MarketWatch story was not opened, and the figure rests on unnamed sources.
importance_line: What changed is that a second report eased the previous day's revenue scare around OpenAI, which matters first to savers whose funds hold chip and cloud shares, then to investors weighing OpenAI's reported fundraising at a $1.4 trillion valuation, and the doubt is that the $70 billion comes from unnamed sources and OpenAI had not commented.
summary: BigGo Finance reports that Nvidia and Micron shares rose before the market opened on Friday 9 Oct 2026, after both fell on Thursday, following a Bloomberg report, relayed by Investing.com on Yahoo Finance and citing people familiar with the matter, that OpenAI expects its annualized revenue (recent sales scaled to a full year) to reach or pass $70 billion by the end of 2026, driven chiefly by its business customers. Our 9 Oct 2026 edition carried both that Bloomberg report and the Financial Times figure of about $50 billion behind Thursday's fall.
notes: URL is the Yahoo Finance page (Investing.com carrying Bloomberg) where the facts were read; the pool's MarketWatch original is not openable here. Entry built from several outlets, so source is AI News Desk.
